solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dear wife, perhaps, once thoughtful

parts.note: a former wife (or husband) is an ex
pensive means lost in thought

explanation.surface: A man looks back on a former wife who was once given to deep reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of affection for the wife, but it is the definition in its sense of costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly or high-priced is a synonym.

clue.text: Make first of episodes appear rather novel

indicators.note: first of tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A writer is urged to make the first episode seem fresh and original.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, a plain synonym for gaining wages.

clue.text: Baseball player that can hold his drink?

definitions.meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter
a jug holds a drink, playing on the idiom for a person who stays sober

explanation.surface: Is there a baseball star who can drink a lot without getting drunk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold his drink' suggests a person who is not easily drunk; here it means a container of liquid, a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseball player who throws to the batter has this title, and a large jug for liquid is also called one.

clue.text: Catch insects regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word insects, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to trap bugs routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something, such as a fish or butterfly, is to trap it in mesh, a synonym.

clue.text: Country is supported by king after uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported by means having the other piece underneath
after uprising tells us the king's name goes upwards, read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch

explanation.surface: A nation is propped up by its monarch after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear is Shakespeare's monarch; in a down entry 'after uprising' reads him upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern state is an example of a country.

clue.text: One order in forty seen out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of forty seen are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A single instruction among forty has been observed being disobeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges FORTYSEEN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a military drill command telling soldiers to look straight ahead, so it is one example of an order.

clue.text: Task for someone with a lot of patience

definitions.meaning: a piece of work to be done

definitions.text: someone with a lot of patience
definitions.meaning: the biblical figure famous for enduring every trial patiently

explanation.surface: A piece of work suited to a very patient person.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work, and the Old Testament sufferer gives us the phrase 'the patience of' him.

clue.text: Drink something very cold at end of hot month? Not half!

indicators.note: at end of places the cold item after the shortened month
not half tells us to keep only the first half of the month's name

parts.note: July is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Fancy an iced drink at the end of a sweltering summer month? Not half!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'definitely', but here it halves JULY to JU, which is followed by ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit juice is a type of drink, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Spirit — type unknown?

parts.note: a brand is a type or make of product
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A query about some liquor whose variety nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: This distilled wine is an example of a spirit.

clue.text: A revolutionary device — whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: a revolving machine part is a device that spins round, so the definition itself supplies the word, which reads identically from either end

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: whichever way you look at it says the word reads the same from left or right

parts.note: a revolving machine part is a device that spins round, so the definition itself supplies the word, which reads identically from either end

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking invention, however you view it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a radical idea, but it means something that spins round.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine part that turns about an axis is a revolving device.

clue.text: The New World overlooked by a married girl

indicators.note: overlooked by means the following letters are ignored, so they are left off the front

parts.note: the Americas were called the New World by Europeans

explanation.surface: A young married woman ignores the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked by' removes A and M (married) from AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Cheer runners crossing street in Derbyshire town

indicators.note: crossing means the cheer spans the street, which sits within it

parts.note: the field is everyone running in a race

explanation.surface: Spectators applaud race runners as they cross a street in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is a county in the English Midlands; the field is the whole set of runners in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town, famous for its crooked church spire, is in Derbyshire.

clue.text: Someone prodding boss in card game

parts.note: a stud is a raised boss or knob on a surface
a poker is one who pokes or prods

explanation.surface: Someone is jabbing the boss during a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager; it is a decorative knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a form of the gambling card game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Language that's somewhat absurd, unfortunately

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a choice of words is rather ridiculous, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'that's', but that word is a link joining the definition to the wordplay; 'Language' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the national tongue of Pakistan, an example of a language.

clue.text: Beer maybe with no head to leak out slowly

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter of the drink word is dropped

parts.note: beer is an example of booze, alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Flat beer without its froth seeps out slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests the froth on beer, but it means the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To seep or trickle out gradually is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Most bizarre enthusiasm about a new island

indicators.note: about means the enthusiasm word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: zest means keen enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Someone shows the oddest eagerness for a newly found island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A, N and I inside ZEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of zany, meaning wacky or outlandish, matches most bizarre.

clue.text: River in Kent or sea lane

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
a lane is a way or path

explanation.surface: A list of waterways: a Kentish river or a shipping lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This river flows through Kent to the Thames estuary at Sheerness.

clue.text: Fifty-one pounds held in cash

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Fifty-one pounds kept as banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' looks like a containment signal but is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets kept as money rather than property are described as liquid, readily available funds.

clue.text: Sang and let rip — it could be extremely loud

indicators.note: could be says the letters of sang, let rip and it can be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A singer belted out a song that may well have been deafening.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise so loud it seems to crack the eardrums is deafening, extremely loud.

clue.text: Mahler composed, not Handel, primarily in this kingdom

indicators.note: composed says the composer's name is rearranged
primarily means the first letter of Handel, which is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Mahler wrote music, rather than Handel, in this realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the first letter of Handel (H) from MAHLER and 'composed' rearranges the remaining AMLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain ruled by a monarch, a synonym for a kingdom.

clue.text: Son breaking sailor's old ruler

indicators.note: breaking means the son letter breaks into the middle of the sailor word

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A son smashes a sailor's antique ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick; it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor of Russia before 1917 was an autocratic monarch, an old ruler.

clue.text: Share with mediocre journalist

parts.note: a hack is a poor-quality writer for newspapers

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor shares out work with a second-rate reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A whack is informal for a portion, as in a fair whack of the profits.

clue.text: Don't consume so much — it's futile

definitions.meaning: advice to cut back, read as two words: employ a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Advice to cut back on consumption is dismissed as pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile and pointless are synonyms, and the instruction to consume less splits into two words.

clue.text: On radio second person is a wool producer

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun in grammar

explanation.surface: A broadcaster declares that a second guest farms wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep grows a fleece, so it is a producer of wool.

clue.text: Vegetable they finally selected in the morning

indicators.note: finally means taking the last letter of the word they

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: They picked out the vegetable in the morning at last.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy tuber is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Dog looking so embarrassed by me?

parts.note: blushing makes the face red
the setter is the crossword's author, speaking as me

explanation.surface: The setter wonders if a dog looks ashamed of its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword compilers often refer to themselves as 'me' or 'I', meaning SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish gundog breed with a chestnut coat is a dog.
